rationale: When step 7 of 10 fails due to an unexpected execution error or corrupted environment state during risky package detonation, restarting completely from fresh wastes significant compute and time re-running deterministic initialization steps 1 through 6. Conversely, naive resumption carries corrupted intermediate artifacts forward. Rolling back to the microVM snapshot captured immediately after step 6 provides optimal trade-offs: it restores a known clean, verified state instantaneously without host re-provisioning overhead, isolates the transient failure, and enables safe retry with alternative execution parameters.
